aggregated_directions.explanation: It appears that the feature “lights up” on a particular subword‐chunk that nearly always occurs as the internal (or “middle”) fragment of compound words. In many examples—whether in scientific terms (as in complex chemical names), in programming and query language tokens (such as parts of “substr” or “computer”), or in mixed technical text—it is the central morphemic unit (for example, the “put” in “computer”) that is isolated. In short, the feature is sensitive to and conveys the semantic and structural importance of a frequently occurring internal substring that helps tie together otherwise disparate compound or morphologically complex words.

Developers rely on the substr function to extract key portions of text.
During the lab experiment, the chlorofluorocarbon sample exhibited unusual behavior.
A malfunction in the supercomputer halted all processing tasks.
The microprocessor's design emphasizes efficient data transfer.
Engineers incorporated a substrate sensor into the device for better stability.
The state-of-the-art computer system outperformed its predecessors.
He recently added several improvements to his substr-focused library.
Research on the fluorocarbon molecule revealed significant energy absorption.
The microcontroller integrates a microprocessor that handles all computational tasks.
The feature activates on the midsection 'put' within 'computer', showing its focus on internal chunks.
It clearly isolates the central part 'chem' in 'biochemistry', conforming to the expected pattern.
When processing 'substrate', the feature lights up the internal fragment, demonstrating compound sensitivity.
In words like 'photograph', the activation is concentrated on the middle segment 'graph', emphasizing semantic centrality.
The system lights up the portion 'miss' in 'transmission', pinpointing the internal morpheme.
During analysis, the core 'put' in 'computer' is precisely highlighted as the internal binding element.
The model detects the mid-chunk in complex terms, as seen with the internal segment of 'biochemical'.
It identifies the linking morpheme in compound words, such as the middle part of 'substring'.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that the feature “lights up” on a particular subword‐chunk that nearly always occurs as the internal (or “middle”) fragment of compound words. In many examples—whether in scientific terms (as in complex chemical names), in programming and query language tokens (such as parts of “substr” or “computer”), or in mixed technical text—it is the central morphemic unit (for example, the “put” in “computer”) that is isolated. In short, the feature is sensitive to and conveys the semantic and structural importance of a frequently occurring internal substring that helps tie together otherwise disparate compound or morphologically complex words.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature has learned to “light‐up” on relational or linking words—the small connectors (often prepositions like “of” or verbs such as “use”) that signal an association between an entity and its property, parameter, or component. In many of these high‐activation examples (whether legal descriptions, technical setup instructions, programming code, or financial explanations), the feature is triggered when the text shifts into a mode of specifying relationships or attributes (for example, linking a value to an environment or a property to an object). In short, the feature represents the abstract notion of relational “glue” in structured, explanatory text that marks the connection between a subject and its modifiers or arguments.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that the feature “lights up” on a particular subword‐chunk that nearly always occurs as the internal (or “middle”) fragment of compound words. In many examples—whether in scientific terms (as in complex chemical names), in programming and query language tokens (such as parts of “substr” or “computer”), or in mixed technical text—it is the central morphemic unit (for example, the “put” in “computer”) that is isolated. In short, the feature is sensitive to and conveys the semantic and structural importance of a frequently occurring internal substring that helps tie together otherwise disparate compound or morphologically complex words.

results.text: The feature activates on the midsection 'put' within 'computer', showing its focus on internal chunks.
It clearly isolates the central part 'chem' in 'biochemistry', conforming to the expected pattern.
When processing 'substrate', the feature lights up the internal fragment, demonstrating compound sensitivity.
In words like 'photograph', the activation is concentrated on the middle segment 'graph', emphasizing semantic centrality.
The system lights up the portion 'miss' in 'transmission', pinpointing the internal morpheme.
During analysis, the core 'put' in 'computer' is precisely highlighted as the internal binding element.
The model detects the mid-chunk in complex terms, as seen with the internal segment of 'biochemical'.
It identifies the linking morpheme in compound words, such as the middle part of 'substring'.
Activation in 'transformer' is centered on the internal fragment 'form', aligning with the explanation.
The internal segment in a mixed technical term is highlighted, much like the isolated middle token in 'substrate'.
The activation spreads over the entire word 'computer' without isolating a central fragment.
In this example, the feature lights up the beginning 'comp' in 'computer', missing the internal focus.
The highlighted segment appears at the end of 'network', contradicting the focus on internal substrings.
Rather than a middle fragment, the activation covers the entire token of a simple word like 'apple'.
The system mistakenly isolates the prefix 'trans' in 'transition', which is not the internal component.
Instead of highlighting a core morpheme, the feature lights up the whole term 'chemical'.
The activation targets the starting fragment in 'autonomous', ignoring the expected internal element.
In this case, the feature misfires by highlighting only the last part of 'cryptograph', not its center.
The entire compound word 'computer' is lit without distinguishing the central 'put'.
Activation occurs on an external segment of 'formless', rather than the internal connecting morpheme.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that the feature “lights up” on a particular subword‐chunk that nearly always occurs as the internal (or “middle”) fragment of compound words. In many examples—whether in scientific terms (as in complex chemical names), in programming and query language tokens (such as parts of “substr” or “computer”), or in mixed technical text—it is the central morphemic unit (for example, the “put” in “computer”) that is isolated. In short, the feature is sensitive to and conveys the semantic and structural importance of a frequently occurring internal substring that helps tie together otherwise disparate compound or morphologically complex words.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature has learned to “light‐up” on relational or linking words—the small connectors (often prepositions like “of” or verbs such as “use”) that signal an association between an entity and its property, parameter, or component. In many of these high‐activation examples (whether legal descriptions, technical setup instructions, programming code, or financial explanations), the feature is triggered when the text shifts into a mode of specifying relationships or attributes (for example, linking a value to an environment or a property to an object). In short, the feature represents the abstract notion of relational “glue” in structured, explanatory text that marks the connection between a subject and its modifiers or arguments.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature has learned to “light‐up” on relational or linking words—the small connectors (often prepositions like “of” or verbs such as “use”) that signal an association between an entity and its property, parameter, or component. In many of these high‐activation examples (whether legal descriptions, technical setup instructions, programming code, or financial explanations), the feature is triggered when the text shifts into a mode of specifying relationships or attributes (for example, linking a value to an environment or a property to an object). In short, the feature represents the abstract notion of relational “glue” in structured, explanatory text that marks the connection between a subject and its modifiers or arguments.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature has learned to “light‐up” on relational or linking words—the small connectors (often prepositions like “of” or verbs such as “use”) that signal an association between an entity and its property, parameter, or component. In many of these high‐activation examples (whether legal descriptions, technical setup instructions, programming code, or financial explanations), the feature is triggered when the text shifts into a mode of specifying relationships or attributes (for example, linking a value to an environment or a property to an object). In short, the feature represents the abstract notion of relational “glue” in structured, explanatory text that marks the connection between a subject and its modifiers or arguments.
